question: Should OpenClaw pursue a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract for horizontally scaled deployments, treat Redis/BullMQ orchestration as an external/plugin pattern, or defer the broad design to narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend boundary, worker failure semantics, credentials, config shape, observability, deployment support, and core-versus-plugin ownership require maintainer product and architecture intent.

options.title: Design backend-neutral contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

options.title: Document external pattern
options.body: Keep core single-process for now and document ScalyClaw/BullMQ-style orchestration as an external deployment or plugin pattern without adding core surfaces.

options.title: Defer To Narrower Trackers
options.body: Use the cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, and database abstraction issues to settle individual boundaries before revisiting a broad job orchestration layer.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, and observability before any Redis/BullMQ-specific code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined live issue-review signal and current queue/cron architecture history for choosing the product boundary.
